businessModel: Donations and volunteer work; no commercial product
updateCadence: A few releases per year; Qt WebEngine updates follow Qt/distro schedule
summary: qutebrowser is a Python/Qt browser controlled with vim-like keys, a command line and hints. It is deeply configurable through config.py and userscripts, but is limited by Qt WebEngine and has no extension store, sync or mobile app.
bestFor: Vim users who want a keyboard-only browser
People who like to configure everything in a text file
Tiling-WM users who want minimal chrome
notFor: People who rely on browser extensions or sync
Anyone who needs strict Chromium-level patch timing

pros.title: True keyboard workflow
pros.detail: Hints, modes, a command line and vim-like bindings cover almost everything without a mouse.

pros.title: Deep configuration
pros.detail: config.py plus per-domain settings, custom CSS and userscripts allow fine control.

pros.title: Built-in ad blocking
pros.detail: Supports ABP-style filter lists, using Brave adblock via python-adblock when installed, plus host blocking.

pros.title: Modern rendering
pros.detail: Qt WebEngine means current Chromium-class compatibility and DevTools.

pros.title: No telemetry
pros.detail: Independent volunteer project with no tracking or accounts.

cons.title: No extensions
cons.detail: No WebExtensions; only Greasemonkey-style userscripts and external scripts.

cons.title: No sync or password manager
cons.detail: Relies on userscripts for Bitwarden/pass/KeePassXC; no built-in sync.

cons.title: Qt WebEngine lag
cons.detail: Security fixes depend on Qt releases and distro packaging, which can trail Chrome.

cons.title: Steep learning curve
cons.detail: Modal keybindings are unfamiliar to non-vim users.

faq.q: Does qutebrowser support Chrome or Firefox extensions?
faq.a: No. It supports Greasemonkey-style userscripts and external scripts, not WebExtensions.
Qt WebEngine, which is Chromium-based. The old QtWebKit backend was removed.

faq.q: Is there a Windows or macOS build?
faq.a: Yes, official builds exist; the 3.7.0 Windows/macOS releases ship Qt 6.11.0.

v3.7.0: Qt 6.11 bundles on Windows/macOS; quickmark/bookmark reload commands

switching.note: Bookmark import is limited (e.g. import script); config migration is manual.

spec.drm: Widevine only if system Qt WebEngine and CDM are available
spec.codecs: Depends on Qt WebEngine build (proprietary codecs often in distro builds)
spec.sandbox: Chromium sandbox via Qt WebEngine (can be disabled by setting)
spec.patchLag: Follows Qt WebEngine and distro updates

jsSpeed: V8 via Qt WebEngine; Chromium-class speed
graphics: GPU raster on Linux, flags sometimes needed
installSize: Qt WebEngine adds roughly Chromium-sized deps
blocking: ABP lists + hosts; no cosmetic filtering
securityHardening: Chromium sandbox/site isolation via Qt WebEngine
patchSpeed: Lags Chromium via Qt WebEngine cadence
